newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Futures fell shaky Australian stocks by close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Futures fell shaky Australian stocks by close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2387 -32 US 30yr cl 6.96 +0.02
10yrbond futs 91.950 -0.070 Gold NY 347.75 Lon fix 351.40
*Stocks slip away as futures fade, News Corp leads losers after Heritage deal, PNG stocks rebound. Vol 424.41 million, value A$1.17 bln, 1,139 stocks traded, 349 steady, 212 up, 578 down.
Australian shares closed lower on Tuesday, the market slipping away in the afternoon in line with a rapidly fading futures market.
Media major News Corp was the featured loser among the leaders as traders voiced their disapproval of the company's US$1.35 billion Heritage buy.
By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 23.1 points lower at 2,404.3.
The March share index futures contract was 32 points lower at 2,387, a 17.3 point discount to the underlying index.

Yesterday's big losers, the Papua New Guinea-linked stocks, recouped some of Monday's losses as fears over political instability in the country diminished, although they eased off their highs with the broader market by the close.

Government-controlled mining investor Orogen Minerals dived 22 cents to an intraday low of A$2.98 before finding support and climbing to a high of A$3.26. It then eased with the broader market to end steady at A$3.20.
Oilsearch ended up 10 cents at A$2.70, Lihir Gold shares closed up two cents at A$2.12, while Niugini Mining added four cents to A$3.00.
The broader market was set for a rangebound day until the last hour of trading when sellers slugged the March share futures contract, dragging the underlying market down with it.
"Futures came off in the last hour or so and that cut most of them back," said a Sydney-based broker, adding that nerves over the U.S. appeared to be the likely cause given the dearth of local news.
"I can only put it down to U.S. concerns. There are still some worries over there."
Others also noted the lack of local impetus, saying the market ran out of puff in the afternoon.
"It slowed down quite a bit and was a very patchy day," said a dealer at a Perth-based brokerage.
News Corp proved a millstone with investors unhappy about the issue of further shares to support Rupert Murdoch's spending spree. Its shares closed 3.3 percent lower at A$6.36.
Packaging group Amcor also weighed on the index, going ex-dividend 18 cents and closing 32 cents lower at A$8.28. while golds disapointed, the gold index losing 1.9 percent.
Grand Hotel Group topped turnover lists with 39.7 million securities traded, the bulk of it in one line through County Natwest Securities at A$2.05 per share.
Brokers said the trade appeared to be the 39 percent stake acquired by Tuan Sing Holdings in January.
Building materials group Boral and retailer Woolworths featured in turnover lists with 10 million and 9.8 million shares traded respectively.

Brokers said there had been talk of Macquarie Equities doing a number of portfolio trades and they featured with a line of 8.3 million Boral shares specialled at a price of A$3.81 each and a line of 7.46 million Woolworths shares at A$3.665 each.
Boral shares ended eight cents lower at A$3.70, while Woolworths closed five cents lower at A$3.55.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 38 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was heavy while options trade also picked up in line with an active underlying market.
Total options traded 42,639 (23,751)
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 11,417 (23,751)

In other local markets, Australian bonds looked fairly heavy at the close as traders braced for another rough ride in after hours trading against the back drop of twitchy U.S. Treasury market. By 5.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.98 percent, just up on Monday's 7.97 percent.

Offshore sellers tore 3/4 cent off the Australian dollar Tuesday, snapping important support and possibly putting paid to its recent uptrend. By 5.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), the dollar had found a temporary haven at US$0.7895/00 after recoiling from an early US$0.7925/30 and US$0.7974/79 late here Monday.
